lead_headline: Restaurant tracker crosses closure threshold with 35 shutdown leads vs 32 openings—first closure majority since launch—as March culling intensifies

restaurant.blurb: 6 new leads today push active count to 67 (32 openings, 35 closures)—closure majority widens as backfill detections accelerate. Opening side: Paperboy Denver debuts Highlands brunch outpost (Austin's first out-of-state expansion), Black Rock Coffee lands 13th Denver location (Overland), Wash Park Social replaces Wash Park Grille under new operator. Closure drag: Chances Grill shuts Union Station nightclub (1523 Market St, multi-floor Caribbean concept), third Dairy Queen closure surfaces (Belleview Ave Littleton, mirroring Sheridan Boulevard Westminster shutdowns). Geographic note: Union Station opening cluster from early-week (Mendocino, C Burger, Ogo) gives way to neighborhood scatter—today's leads span Highlands, Overland, Washington Park. Closure-to-opening ratio hits 1.09:1, highest imbalance yet; backlog now filling from delayed 2025 shutdowns vs real-time March detections.

foreclosure.blurb: 42 filings this week hold 40% above prior week's 30-case floor, sustaining March volatility as $57M Arapahoe commercial outlier (2038 S Vaughn) drags $71M aggregate—next-largest filing plummets to $795K Weld County, exposing single-case concentration risk.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extend March's unprecedented blackout to 26 consecutive days without filings—longest silence in tracker history. Monthly tally flatlined at zero through full four weeks, erasing January-February's 12/week baseline. No pending applications visible across Denver, Arapahoe, Boulder, Jefferson metro counties. Seasonal hypothesis: operators may batch Q2 submissions for April 1 quarterly window targeting summer patio season, but 26-day void suggests systemic reporting lag vs typical pre-filing chatter. April 1-7 watch period critical—if drought persists, points to state database delays or regulatory process changes vs demand collapse.

reputation.blurb: 2 mentions today (outdoor gear retailer closure, Windsor King Soopers on social) lift 7-day total to 52—up 33% from prior week's 39, fifth straight week above 40-mention floor. Denver Post dominates with 19 pickups (37% share), Instagram delivers 10, Facebook and Hoodline tie at 6 each. Notable coverage: Wilderness Exchange 26-year closure (Post/SGB Media crossover), Republic Plaza deadline miss (Hoodline), escape room brewery conversion (Post). Source diversification improves vs yesterday: Post share drops from 41% to 37%, Instagram holds steady at 19%—social platforms plus Post still command 71% of volume but concentration eases slightly.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 today (1 new, 0 canceled) edges MTD to +49 (+2.0/day), 90-day cumulative to +118 (+1.3/day). Last 7 days deliver +21 net (28 new, 7 canceled) vs prior week's +19—acquisition accelerates to 4.0/day from prior week's 3.6, but cancellations tick up to 1.0/day from 0.9. Two-week pattern: steady 4+/day new subscriber flow since March 12 (only two zero-acquisition days), but churn creeps upward—7 cancels this week vs 6 last week vs 4 in early-March window. March pacing toward +52 net if final 5 days match current 2.0/day rate—would mark 30% gain over February baseline but trails explosive early-month 2.5/day peaks. Retention slippage (1.0/day cancel rate) offsets otherwise healthy acquisition momentum.
